done_when: init.protect drops required checks that no remaining workflow produces, names the repo from the origin remote explicitly in every gh api call, and a test proves each

findings.body: An absolute local origin bypasses the refusal and sends both protection requests using `{owner}/{repo}`. With `GH_REPO` pointing elsewhere, this can modify an unrelated repository because [gh resolves those placeholders from its repository context](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api). Remove the production exception and refuse unresolved origins. Tests can use GitHub fetch URLs with local push URLs, as the new test already does at tests/test_fix_forge_s_branch_protection_keeps_required.py:65–66.
findings.title: Simpler: test-only repository fallback → refuse unresolved origins

findings.body: The exact comparison rejects `jobs: # required checks`, although comments are valid [YAML syntax](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#66-comments). If a deleted workflow declares `keep-check` and a surviving workflow uses that commented header to declare the same job, the surviving producer is invisible and protection drops a live requirement. Conversely, a commented header in the deleted workflow leaves its obsolete checks required. Handle comments and valid indentation when discovering jobs. This is P2 under the requested edge-case rule; the supplied generated-workflow scenario is covered.
findings.title: Recognize commented jobs headers before removing required checks

why: Forge's branch protection keeps required checks whose workflows a migration deletes, which blocks every later pull request once admins are enforced, and with two remotes and no gh default it can protect the wrong repo
